hook.text: You buy a $1,000 watch without thinking about what else $1,000 could do. A vacation, a month of rent, an investment.

buildup.text: Opportunity cost neglect: we rarely consider what we're giving up when we spend. The alternatives stay invisible.

discovery.text: Frederick's research showed that explicitly mentioning alternatives — 'this OR a weekend trip' — reduced purchase.

twist.text: Opportunity Cost Neglect shows that intuition alone misreads how people actually choose.

climax.text: Opportunity Cost Neglect matters because better design changes real decisions.

punchline.text: Every purchase is a trade. See the other side.

quiz.question: What is opportunity cost neglect?
options: Failing to consider alternative uses of money when spending
Investing in too many opportunities at once
